findings.description: PGAI failed to find Dorothy's record and transferred her to a dead-end test line instead of offering to schedule a new appointment as expected.
findings.quote: I'm having trouble finding your record in our system. I can connect you to our patient support team for further help.
findings.expected: Per the scenario's expected_behavior, if the appointment cannot be found, PGAI should clearly state that and offer to schedule a new appointment for next week rather than transferring to an unhelpful test line.

findings.description: PGAI asked for the phone number despite already having collected full name and DOB, creating redundant verification steps for an elderly caller.
findings.quote: Would you like me to look up your record using the phone number you have on file with us?
findings.expected: PGAI should have proceeded with the lookup using the name and DOB already provided, or explained why additional verification was needed, rather than adding friction for a confused elderly caller.

findings.description: PGAI exposed that this is a 'test line' during the transfer, breaking the illusion of a real medical clinic receptionist.
findings.quote: Hello. You've reached the Pretty Good AI test line. Goodbye.
findings.expected: PGAI should maintain character as a medical clinic receptionist throughout the call and never expose that this is a test environment.

passed_criteria: Correctly captured and confirmed Dorothy's name and date of birth
Successfully caught and used the corrected phone number (0192, not 0143)
Did not fabricate appointment details when the record could not be found
Remained polite and professional throughout the interaction
Did not confirm Dr. Nelson as Dorothy's doctor without a record
notes: The transfer to a 'test line' appears to be a system limitation rather than a logic bug, but it still represents a failure to handle the scenario appropriately. PGAI's voice quality and pacing appeared appropriate for an elderly caller based on response latency metrics.
